testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: You cannot drink alcohol within ____ before starting work.
questions.explanation: Commercial drivers cannot drink any alcohol within four hours before starting work.

questions.question: Non-front tires on a commercial vehicle must have a tread depth of at least ____.
questions.explanation: Front tires need 4/32 of an inch tread depth. Other tires need 2/32 of an inch.

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brake systems are too loud.
Other brake systems are hard to find.

questions.explanation: Air brakes are safe and effective for stopping large, heavy vehicles when used and maintained properly.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, start by:

options.text: Turning the wheel in the direction you want to go.
Turning the wheel in the opposite direction.
Turning the wheel as far as it will go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning the wheel in the opposite direction.
questions.explanation: Start by turning the wheel opposite to where you want the trailer to go. Then reverse the wheel direction to follow the trailer.

questions.question: When driving downhill, brake until you reach ____ below your safe speed, then release the brake.
questions.explanation: Brake until your speed is 5 mph below your safe speed, then release the brake. Repeat this process.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer:

options.text: You cannot back in a straight line.
Do not correct drift until you are far off course.
Pull forward often to reposition the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward often to reposition the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Pull forward to reposition whenever needed. Correct drift right away by turning the wheel toward the drift.

questions.question: After an accident, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Move your vehicle to the side of the road

questions.explanation: Protect the area, call authorities, help the injured, get information, and report the accident. Leaving the scene can cost you your license.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle parked:

options.text: Do not apply brakes if the vehicle is in neutral.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when parked. Chock the wheels if needed.

questions.question: When backing up, follow a turning trailer by:

options.text: Doing nothing. The vehicle will follow naturally.
Turning the wheel even harder in the same direction.

questions.explanation: Start by turning the wheel opposite to the turn. Once the trailer starts turning, reverse the wheel direction to follow it.

questions.question: If you begin a left turn before reaching the center of an intersection, you may:

options.text: Hit other vehicles with the left side of your vehicle.
Expect other drivers to move for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hit other vehicles with the left side of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Reach the center of the intersection before turning left. Turning too early can cause the left side of your vehicle to hit another vehicle.

questions.question: Cargo with a high center of gravity:

options.text: Can make a vehicle tip over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make a vehicle tip over.
questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip over. Always keep cargo weight as low as possible.

questions.question: If a tire fails, you should:
questions.explanation: Braking after a tire fails can cause you to lose control. Avoid using the brakes until your vehicle slows down.

questions.question: When driving in winter, what should receive extra attention during a pre-trip inspection?
questions.explanation: Before winter driving, check the coolant and antifreeze levels, defrosting and heating equipment, wiper blades, windshield washer, tires, tire chains, lights, reflectors, windows, mirrors, handholds, steps, deck plates, radiator shuttles, winterfront, and exhaust system.

questions.question: When braking with ABS, you should:

options.text: Brake harder than with other braking systems.

questions.explanation: With an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), brake the same way you would with any other braking system.

questions.question: A truck tractor built after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection should include:
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check the engine oil level, radiator coolant level, and condition of the hoses.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Is a good way to stay awake on long trips.

questions.explanation: Rough acceleration can damage the vehicle. Always accelerate smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you while driving a large vehicle, do all of the following except:
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase your following distance and avoid quick moves. Do not increase your speed or flash your brake lights.

questions.question: If you notice an unusual noise or feeling while driving, you should:

options.text: Assume it is not a problem and continue driving.
Hope the vehicle is fine until another driver takes over.
Check it out to find the right solution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check it out to find the right solution.
questions.explanation: If you see, hear, smell, or feel anything unusual while driving, have it checked.

questions.question: When driving long distances, take a break every ____ to avoid getting too tired.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on long trips, take a break at least every two hours or 100 miles.

questions.question: If a police officer asks you to take a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) test:

options.text: You can refuse without any penalty.
You can refuse but will have to pay a $50 fine.
You will lose your CDL if you refuse.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will lose your CDL if you refuse.
questions.explanation: Most states have an Implied Consent Law. This means that by driving on state roads, you agree to take a drug or alcohol test if a police officer asks. If you refuse, you will lose your driving privileges. Learn the laws for every state where you drive.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections are:

options.text: Needed only for trips longer than 100 miles.

questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require you to inspect your vehicle before every trip, no matter how long the trip is.

questions.question: What is the best advice for driving in fog?

options.text: Avoid driving in fog if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving in fog if possible.
questions.explanation: Driving in fog is dangerous and should be avoided when possible. If you must drive in fog, turn on your low beam headlights and fog lights, even during the day.

questions.question: If you realize you may be late to your destination, you should:
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, manage your stress. If you will be late, take a deep breath and accept the situation while driving at a safe speed.

questions.question: In hot weather, spots where tar is bleeding on the pavement:

options.text: Have the same traction as the rest of the road.
Have more traction than the rest of the road.

questions.explanation: In very hot weather, tar in road pavement rises to the surface, or "bleeds." Watch for these areas because they are very slippery.

questions.question: When driving on a surface with poor traction, you should accelerate slowly:

options.text: Because it is always good to accelerate slowly.
To keep from losing control of the vehicle.
So you don't go faster than the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep from losing control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate slowly in poor traction conditions, such as rain or snow, to avoid losing control of your vehicle.

questions.question: An Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) does NOT need to include which of the following?
questions.explanation: An Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) must include the dates of a trip and the total distance traveled. It should also include fuel purchase information. It does not need to include the number of vehicles passed.

questions.question: When putting out an electrical fire, you should:
questions.explanation: B:C fire extinguishers work on electrical fires and burning liquids. Do not use water on an electrical fire.

questions.question: Wheels with welding repairs are:

options.text: Safe if a professional did the repairs.
Safe if the repair looks solid.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims that have been welded are not safe. Replace them before driving the vehicle.

questions.question: Poor weight balance in a trailer:
questions.explanation: Poor weight balance in a trailer makes handling unsafe. Too much or too little weight on the front axle makes steering difficult. Distribute weight evenly from front to back and side to side. Keep weight as low as possible.

questions.question: What is a tire load?

options.text: The minimum safe weight a tire can carry
The maximum safe weight a tire can carry

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
questions.explanation: Tire load is the maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a certain pressure.

questions.question: When should you check cargo being transported?

options.text: Before the trip and again within the first 50 miles

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the trip and again within the first 50 miles
questions.explanation: Check cargo before you start and again within the first 50 miles. Also check it every three hours or 150 miles after that. The driver is responsible for keeping cargo secure the entire trip.

questions.question: If driving through flowing water or a large puddle, you should:

options.text: Try to stop in the water

questions.explanation: Avoid driving through water if possible. If you must drive through it, slow down, shift to a low gear, and gently apply the brakes. This keeps water and mud out of the brake system.

questions.question: When operating a vehicle with a dual air brake system, the driver should:

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up before driving
Let the air compressor build up a minimum of 100 psi in both brake systems before driving
Begin driving right after the vehicle starts

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the air compressor build up a minimum of 100 psi in both brake systems before driving
questions.explanation: Before driving, allow the air compressor to build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary brake systems. Watch the air pressure gauges.

questions.question: When exiting a vehicle, you must maintain ____ with your vehicle at all times.
questions.explanation: Face the vehicle and keep three points of contact as you exit. On a bus, hold the handrail. Not doing this correctly can cause you to fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: To ensure normal stopping power with a front brake limiting valve, you should:
questions.explanation: Some vehicles have a brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings. Keep it on "normal" for full stopping power. The "slippery" setting reduces stopping power.

questions.question: When driving on a long downhill slope, you should brake by:

options.text: Mostly using the brakes and sometimes downshifting
Downshifting and then using the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting and then using the brakes
questions.explanation: On a long downgrade, shift to a lower gear first, then use the brakes. Using only brakes can cause them to overheat and fail. The engine's braking power in a lower gear is the main way to control your speed.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Wet ice forms when warm weather slightly melts the ice. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: Your horn should be used to:

options.text: Tell other drivers that you are angry
Warn other drivers that you are near

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other drivers that you are near
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn others of your presence. Only use it when necessary, since it may startle other drivers.

questions.question: If confronted by an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact to communicate with them
Not move out of their path

questions.explanation: If confronted by an aggressive driver, get out of their way if you can. Do not make eye contact, as this may provoke them. Do not let them provoke you.

questions.question: What do you need to do to inspect slack adjusters on S-cam brakes?

options.text: Park on a hill and test the brakes.
Put on gloves and push in the slack adjusters.
Chock the wheels and disengage the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Chock the wheels and disengage the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Park on level ground. Set wheel chocks and disengage the parking brake. Pull each slack adjuster to check it. It should not move more than one inch. If it moves more than one inch, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: How much should you reduce your speed when driving on a wet road?
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed when the road is wet. Slow down by about one-third of your normal speed on wet roads.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, you should ensure that the ____ come on automatically when air pressure falls below 45 psi.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes should come on automatically when air tank pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. Test this by chocking the wheels and releasing air from the brake system. Press and release the brake pedal until pressure drops. The parking brake valve should pop out and spring brakes should engage.

questions.question: When leaving a vehicle unattended, a driver should:

options.text: Only set the parking brake if the vehicle is parked on a slope.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: How should you brake if your vehicle's ABS is not working?

options.text: Brake normally, as you will still have functioning brakes.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally, as you will still have functioning brakes.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle will still have normal brakes without ABS. Brake as you normally would. Have your ABS fixed as soon as possible.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may mean they are loose. Check the tightness of the nuts if you see rust in that area.

questions.question: When an S-cam turns inside a brake drum, the S-cam:

options.text: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
Presses the brake shoes against the brake linings.
Presses the brake linings against the wheel axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, the S-cam turns and presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: Having ABS on only one axle:

options.text: Still allows you additional control when braking.
Slows the vehicle, but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Still allows you additional control when braking.
questions.explanation: If ABS is on only the tractor, trailer, or one axle, you still have more control when braking than without ABS. Brake normally.

questions.question: If you have more than one license:

options.text: You may get caught through the states' shared computer network.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may get caught through the states' shared computer network.
questions.explanation: All states share driver information through a computer database to prevent issuing multiple licenses to one person. Having more than one driver license is illegal.

questions.question: A wig wag is:

options.text: A tube that carries air to the brakes.
A type of air brake system.

questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a low pressure warning device. A wig wag is one type. It drops a mechanical arm into your view if air tank pressure drops between 55 and 75 psi.
